ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The waveform on the left in the figure is labeled s1(t), with amplitude +A in the interval from 0 to T/2, and amplitude -A in the interval from T/2 to T. The waveform on the right is labeled s0(t), with amplitude -A in the interval from 0 to T/2, and amplitude +A in the interval from T/2 to T. Therefore the figure shows s0(t) = -s1(t), and the amplitude magnitude of both signals over the entire 0 to T is A. Reasoning: The energy of either signal E = ∫_0^T A^2 dt = A^2 T. The squared Euclidean distance between the two signals d^2 = ∫_0^T [s1(t)-s0(t)]^2 dt. Since s0(t) = -s1(t), s1(t)-s0(t)=2s1(t), so d^2 = ∫_0^T 4A^2 dt = 4A^2T. For an AWGN channel with bilateral noise power spectral density n0/2 and equiprobable binary signals, the minimum error rate is P_b,min = Q(sqrt(d^2/(2n0))) = Q(sqrt(2A^2T/n0)). Using Q(x)=1/2 erfc(x/sqrt(2)), obtain P_b,min = 1/2 erfc(sqrt(A^2T/n0)).
